transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I guess I'm here because... well, ever since those foreclosure notices started coming, I just feel like I’m coming apart at the seams. 

It's getting really bad. I find myself sitting out in my truck crying before work, and I jump every single time the phone rings. It's messing with my job, too. I'm snapping at the apprentices over nothing, and... I'm making these stupid mistakes in the repair bay that I never would’ve made before. I just can't seem to hold it together right now.
Do these feelings seem mostly connected to the foreclosure notices?

Yeah, absolutely. I was functioning totally normally before all this. But once those foreclosure letters and the phone calls started coming in... it just hit me hard. Within a few weeks of getting that first formal notice, everything just started unraveling. My work, my home life... it all just fell apart right after that started.
Since this started, have you been feeling down or depressed?

I wouldn't really say I feel depressed, no. I mean, I'm obviously not happy about the situation, but I don't feel that deep sadness or anything like that. It's more just... this constant panic and stress about losing the house. So, no, not really down, just incredibly wound up and overwhelmed by it all.
Aside from the foreclosure, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many other parts of your life?

No, not really. I mean... it's just the house. Everything else is pretty much fine. I don't sit around worrying about, you know, other stuff in my life. It's literally just the foreclosure. If I didn't have the bank breathing down my neck right now, I wouldn't be worrying at all.
Since the foreclosure started, have you been feeling nervous or anxious most days?

I'm not sure I'd use the word nervous. I haven't really noticed feeling anxious, like in a general way, if that's what you mean. It's really just... what I was saying a minute ago, that heavy stress about the bank taking the house. But no, I wouldn't say I'm just walking around feeling nervous every day.
When the phone rings or you think about the foreclosure, do you feel panicky?

Yeah, absolutely. Every time the phone rings, I jump out of my skin. Ever since those foreclosure notices started showing up, I just feel like I'm coming apart at the seams. I'm sitting in my truck crying before I even clock in for work. And it's bleeding into my job, too. I'm a mechanic, and lately I've been snapping at the apprentices over nothing, making stupid mistakes in the repair bay... things I never would've messed up before this all started. So yeah, thinking about it or getting a call definitely sets me off.
Since this started, have you been having sudden surges of intense fear?
No, I wouldn't call it that. It's not like a sudden wave of fear out of nowhere. It's just that constant, heavy dread about the house. I don't get those sudden panic attacks or anything like that.
Do you feel your reaction to the foreclosure has been more intense than most people would have in the same situation?

I don't really know. I mean, I haven't compared myself to anyone else. But losing your house is a massive deal... I feel like anybody would be a total wreck if they were going through this. So, no, I don't know if my reaction is more intense than what most people would feel. I just know it's really tearing me apart.
Since this started, have you been feeling tense or on edge?

Yeah, I'd say so. Like I said earlier about jumping when the phone rings... I just feel wound up all the time. It's like I can't relax, even when I'm off the clock. My shoulders are always tight, and I'm just waiting for the next piece of bad news.
Since this started, have you been crying because you feel sad or hopeless?

No, I haven't really been crying. I mean, I'm definitely worried sick about the house, but it doesn't really come out as tears. I'm not sitting around crying or feeling hopeless, like I'm just giving up. It's mostly just that constant dread and tension I mentioned.
